verified.title: authorizeBridge treats loopback-peer requests as workstation unless a hard-coded header list matches; unlisted relay headers grant the workstation token
verified.boundary: Remote (unpaired or paired) client reaching the Host via a loopback relay/proxy -> workstation (local:true) authority, which yields the Host master token in hostCall and full workstation actor.
verified.reproduction: A loopback-peer reverse proxy rewrites Host to 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost and forwards a remote request with no cookie and no header in PROXY_HEADERS/RELAY_PREFIX (e.g. x-request-id, x-nginx-proxy). authorizeBridge returns {local:true,token:null}; hostCall then sends the workstation credentials token. Probe run: node --experimental-strip-types scratchpad/review-probes/d4-bridge-probe.mts -> 'relay adds unlisted header x-request-id => {"local":true,"token":null}' and 'x-nginx-proxy' same, while x-forwarded-for is refused. Current configured tunnel is cloudflared quick/named tunnel which adds cf-* headers, so exposure today depends on a non-cloudflared or misconfigured relay.
verified.evidence: src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.ts:10-11 (RELAY_PREFIX / PROXY_HEADERS allowlist of relay markers, deny-list style), :28-30 (local = loopbackHost && loopbackPeer), :40-41 (relayed check only over the listed names), :45 (return local:true, token:null), :90-98 (hostCall uses credentials.token when access.local). Host side accepts Host 127.0.0.1/localhost only (src/lib/bunny-host/http.server.ts:391-392), so the relay must rewrite Host, which is the stated attack precondition.
verified.repair: Invert the check to an allowlist: treat a request as workstation only when it carries no headers beyond a known local set (or only when the Host and Origin match and no Forwarded/X-* family header is present at all). Add a unit test for an arbitrary x-* header on a loopback request, and fail closed when BUNNY_REMOTE_ORIGIN is configured and the peer is loopback.

votes.severityIfReal: HIGH if a loopback relay that adds no listed or prefixed header is exposed (the bypass grants the Host master token and full workstation actor); MEDIUM as currently deployed, because the documented cloudflared tunnel adds cf-* headers and is refused.
votes.reasoning:
The claim is real in the current working tree. Evidence:

1. src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.ts:40 is the only relay check for a loopback request. It tests PROXY_HEADERS, RELAY_PREFIX and two extra names (front-end-https, x-url-scheme). Any other header passes.
2. src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.ts:30 sets local = loopbackHost && loopbackPeer. Line 45 returns {local:true, token:null}, and line 94 then sends the workstation token from hostCredentials() to the Host.
3. I ran scratchpad/review-probes/d4-bridge-probe.mts. Output: x-request-id => {"local":true,"token":null}; x-nginx-proxy => {"local":true,"token":null}. x-forwarded-for is refused.
4. The stated precondition is needed. Host must be 127.0.0.1 or localhost (line 27), and the peer must be loopback (line 28). Stock nginx proxy_pass rewrites Host to the upstream address, adds no X-Forwarded-For by default, and sends no cf-* header. So a plausible misconfigured loopback relay meets every condition.
5. The Origin and sec-fetch-site checks (lines 33-34) are bypassed by a non-browser client that sends neither header. The cookie check (line 44) only matters when a bunny_device cookie is present.

Against refutation: BUNNY_REMOTE.md says the active tunnel is cloudflared, and cloudflared adds cf-ray and cf-connecting-ip, which are in the list. So the documented deployment is not exploitable today. The test at src/lib/bunny-missions/remote-authority.test.ts:945 covers only the listed families, and nothing tests an unlisted header. The deny-list design is therefore incomplete, not intended. The comment at line 39 says any forwarding marker must cause refusal, and this gap contradicts that intent.

Severity: the bypass yields the Host master token, which crosses the boundary the owner set. That fits the HIGH rubric when reachable. It is a conditional gap, so MEDIUM is the fair rating for the current deployment. The fix is an allowlist: a loopback request with any header not from a known local-client set is refused, or a fail-closed check on a Forwarded-style marker plus Host/peer consistency.

The allowlist gap is real in the working tree. Probe (scratchpad/review-probes/skeptic-identity-1/p.mts) with a loopback Host and loopback peer returns {"local":true,"token":null} for unlisted x-request-id and x-nginx-proxy, while cf-ray, x-real-ip and x-forwarded-host are refused. Line 39-40 of src/lib/orch/host-bridge.server.ts says "any forwarding marker" but implements a name allowlist, so the code contradicts its own comment. However the exploit is narrower than the finding states. (1) Origin: if a browser sends the public Origin, line 35 throws "Origin mismatch" (probe confirmed), so the attacker must be a non-browser client or the relay must strip Origin. (2) Host: the relay must rewrite Host to 127.0.0.1 or localhost, which nginx's default proxy_pass does, so that part is plausible. (3) The current cloudflared tunnel adds cf-ray and cf-connecting-ip, which are refused (probe confirmed), and it keeps the public Host, so it is not exploitable today. The path is therefore a non-cloudflared relay that rewrites Host, does not rewrite or strip Origin, and forwards a non-listed header. That is a deployment-conditional defense-in-depth gap, not a demonstrated bypass in the configured deployment. Because the gap is real in the tree, I do not refute it, but I would keep it at MEDIUM and not raise it to HIGH. The finding's REPRO line should add the Origin condition, since a browser remote is blocked by line 35.

verified.title: mutationSequence is not monotonic: a promotion that fails after the rename restores the count, so pre-promotion grants validate again and the unrecorded project change is invisible to the code gates
verified.boundary: Trusted-desktop grant binding (mutationSequence) for staged-change promotion. Crosses store.server.ts mutationSequence, staging.server.ts writePromoted, and manager.server.ts promoteStaged.
verified.reproduction: 1) Device write is staged (its filesystem.write capability run is inserted, count=1). 2) Workstation mints a terminal.exec grant at count=1. 3) Workstation promotes: STAGED->PROMOTING (count=2, grant void), writePromoted renames the phone bytes into the project, then the read-back readFileSync inside writePromoted throws (for example a Windows AV/indexer lock, EBUSY/EPERM). 4) The catch in promoteStaged transitions PROMOTING->FAILED, so the device_staging count drops to 0 and the total returns to 1. 5) The grant from step 2 passes desktopGrantViolation again, and the project file holds the unreviewed phone bytes. No remote_changes row is written on this path (recordRemoteChange only runs after success), so pendingRemoteReview(), the session gate and the code-run gate see nothing to review.
verified.evidence: store.server.ts:151-156 counts runs plus device_staging rows in state PROMOTING/PROMOTED, so the count can decrease. staging.server.ts:160-175 renames before the read-back. manager.server.ts ~2642-2648: the writePromoted failure is caught and transitions PROMOTING->FAILED, and the read-back mismatch branch also goes to FAILED after the file was already replaced. manager.server.ts ~2651-2655 records remote_changes only on success. Probe: scratchpad/review-probes/sequence-rollback.probe.mjs prints 'record: FAILED', 'file now: "phone-authored\n"' and 'grant violation now: NONE'. Also run scratchpad/review-probes/grant-after-promotion.probe.mjs: on the current tree, the success path correctly voids the grant ('Project files changed ...').
verified.repair: Make the trusted-desktop sequence strictly monotonic: keep a persisted counter that increments on every transition into PROMOTING and on every transition into FAILED or PROMOTED after a rename, never a COUNT that can decrease. On any failure after the rename, record a remote_changes row (unacknowledged) for the destination with the bytes' sha, so the next code-run ask lists it, and surface the FAILED state to the workstation as a changed project file.

votes.reasoning:
The claim is real in the current working tree; I did not refute it.

Code evidence:
- store.server.ts:151-156: mutationSequence() = capability_runs count (filesystem.write, terminal.exec, etc.) + device_staging rows in state PROMOTING/PROMOTED. A row that moves PROMOTING->FAILED leaves the count, so the total can fall.
- staging.server.ts:160-175 (writePromoted): renameSync puts the phone bytes at the destination, then the read-back readFileSync runs inside the same function. A throw there happens after the file has already changed.
- manager.server.ts:2641-2644: a writePromoted exception goes to transition(PROMOTING->FAILED) and rethrows. Lines 2646-2649 do the same on a read-back hash mismatch, after the file was already replaced. Neither path writes a remote_changes row; that happens only at 2653 on success.
- desktopGrantViolation (authorization.server.ts:298+) compares grant.mutationSequence against the live count, so a grant minted at count=1 validates again once the count returns to 1.

Probe: I ran scratchpad/review-probes/sequence-rollback.probe.mjs. Output: "file now: "phone-authored\n" record: FAILED", "sequence minted at 1 now 1", "grant violation now: NONE". The probe calls writePromoted and the FAILED transition directly rather than going through promoteStaged, so it demonstrates the counter mechanics, not the full manager path. The code reading covers the rest.

Limits that affect severity and the "unreviewed" wording:
- The trigger is an internal write or read-back exception after rename (for example an AV or indexer lock). The phone cannot cause it directly, so this is not a phone-reachable path to code execution.
- The bytes are not unreviewed in the strict sense. The workstation approved promotion of the reviewed sha256 (readVerified at 2637). What is broken is the time binding: a grant minted before the project changed is accepted over the changed state, and the audit record says FAILED while the file was in fact replaced.
- The reported "grant violation now: NONE" is real. A terminal.exec grant would then run over phone-authored bytes that were never part of its approved state.

Judgement: a real invariant break (grant binding is not monotonic, audit state disagrees with disk) with a plausible but environment-dependent path. MEDIUM fits. A fix would be a monotonic promotion-attempt counter, or counting FAILED rows whose rename happened, plus recording a remote_changes entry on any post-rename failure.

The mechanism is real in the working tree. store.server.ts:151-156 counts device_staging rows in PROMOTING/PROMOTED, so a PROMOTING->FAILED transition lowers the count. manager.server.ts:2643-2647 catches a writePromoted throw and moves PROMOTING->FAILED with no remote_changes row, and the sha-mismatch branch at ~2648-2651 does the same after the rename has already replaced the file. staging.server.ts:160-175 renames before the read-back, so the project file is changed when the read-back throws. Probe sequence-rollback.probe.mjs (run by me, output unchanged): "file now: phone-authored", "record: FAILED", "sequence minted at 1 now 1", "grant violation now: NONE". The grant remains valid over the changed project.

Mitigating facts that keep this at MEDIUM and not higher: the phone cannot trigger it, since promoteStaged requires isTrustedLocalActor and a workstation-approved promotion of the exact reviewed bytes. Triggering it needs a read error right after a successful rename (rare on Windows, though AV locks make it plausible). The bytes were the ones the workstation approved for promotion, so the "unreviewed bytes" wording overstates it. The real defects are that a pre-promotion trusted-desktop grant validates over changed project state, and that the operator sees "Promotion failed" while the file has changed, with no remote_changes entry. The success path does void the grant (grant-after-promotion probe), so the bug is confined to the failure branch. The suggested fix is to keep the count monotonic (for example a separate monotonic counter or a bump on any PROMOTING entry) and to record a remote_changes row whenever the rename happened.
